entities.summary:
Magnus III of Sweden, also known as Magnus Ladulås or Magnus Birgersson, was the King of Sweden from 1275 until his death in 1290. Born in Sweden around 1250, Magnus III was the son of Birger Magnusson, the King of Sweden from 1250 to 1266. He succeeded his father in 1275 and ruled Sweden until his death on December 25, 1290. Magnus III played a crucial role in the political and military history of Sweden, particularly during the Kalmar Union, a union of Denmark, Norway, and Sweden that lasted from 1397 to 1523.

Magnus III expanded Sweden's territories through military conquests, including the conquest of the Danish province of Skåne. He also strengthened the Swedish economy by promoting trade and commerce, particularly with the Hanseatic League, a powerful trading federation that dominated much of Northern Europe during the Middle Ages. Magnus III's reign is also notable for the development of the Swedish language and culture, as he encouraged the use of Swedish as the official language of government and literature.

Magnus III's legacy continued to shape Swedish history long after his death. He was succeeded by his son, Magnus Eriksson, who continued his father's military conquests and expanded Sweden's territories further. Magnus III's influence can also be seen in the development of the Swedish monarchy, which has continued to play a significant role in Swedish politics and society to this day.

Magnus III's significance extends beyond his own reign, as he played a key role in the development of the Kalmar Union and the expansion of Swedish territories. His military conquests and trade agreements with the Hanseatic League helped to establish Sweden as a major power in Northern Europe during the Middle Ages.
